newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- A member of the Springbok rugby management team is facing an investigation after allegedly making racist comments about leading players and public figures.

- Battle lines have been drawn again in the Free State with new premier Ivy Matsepe Casaburri losing the contest yesterday for the provincial leadership of the African National Congress, despite her "deployment" to the province by the ANC's national leadership.
- The political battle around National Party (NP) leader FW de Klerk would intensify, with two powerful factions calling for his axing, senoir party officials said on Sunday.
- As many as eight out of ten veterinarians who graduated in South Africa last year took up positions overseas, Gauteng veterinary services director Malcolm de Bude said.

- South African and European Union diplomats moved at the weekend to avert a potential crisis in Tuesday's cooperation talks as two EU member states threatened to scuttle emerging deals between the two sides, sources close to the process said.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Portnet has all but torpedoed a hotel project, worth about 250 million rand, proposed for the port of Durban.

- The government expects to receive 1,2 billion rand from the sale of a 49-percent stake in the Airports Company, Transport Minister Mac Maharaj said on Friday, as the company's enterprise restructuring committee met for the first time.
- Speculation of a closer tie-up between the Board of Executors (BoE) and newly merged NBS Boland Bank is mounting with all their shares finishing the week markedly stronger on the JSE.

- Lonrho, the British mining and industrial group, has for the first time disclosed in last year's annual report that Terence Wilkinson, its South African-based executive director, earned 336,528 pounds (2.386 million rand) in salary, fees and "benefits in kind". This figure excludes 30,723 pounds tgat Lonrho paid towards Wilkinson's pension.
SAKE BEELD
- The European Union will prevent that the South African mining giant Anglo-American upholds its interest of 26 percent in Lonrho.

- Stocks & Stocks has four black consortiums, which represent several small and medium concerns and chosen as partners for Stocks Hotels and Resorts, will on Monday be listed and will bid for 10 of the country's 40 casino licenses.

- The new chief economist at Sanlam Jac Laubscher said Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's role in implementing the country's new macro-economic plan should not be underestimated. "He is the right person for the right time. A politician with the necessary power to get the plan implemented."
THE STAR

- Free State Premier Dr Ivy Matsepe-Casaburri has been defeated in her bid to lead the ANC in the province, with delegates to the organisation's weekend provincial congress voting in an executive committee seen as overwhelmingly in favour of ousted premier Patrick Lekota.
- The explosive and racist contents of a secret taped conversation between a top South African rugby official and a provincial captain could prove highly damaging to the sport.
- Voluntary severance packages for teachers have cost at least one billion rand so far.

- For the first time since the birth of their 14-month-old tug-of-love son, Lawrie Fraser and Adri Naude are on the same side since the traumatic kidnapping of their baby Timothy, living with his adoptive parents in Malawi on Saturday. The separated coupled have been locked in legal battles over the baby's adoption.
